title: How to Configure Active Directory in Windows Server 2025
summary: Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) is the central authority for identity, authentication, and security policies in a Windows environment. In Windows Server 2025, establishing a Domain Controller remains a strict two-phase process: first, installing the AD DS server role, and second, promoting the server to act as a Domain Controller.
content:
Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) is the central authority for identity, authentication, and security policies in a Windows environment. In Windows Server 2025, establishing a Domain Controller remains a strict two-phase process: first, installing the AD DS server role, and second, promoting the server to act as a Domain Controller.

Before you begin, ensure your server is prepared. You must assign a static IP address, set a permanent hostname (as changing it post-deployment can severely disrupt directory operations), and log in with local administrative privileges.

1.Open the Add Roles and Features Wizard

Launch Server Manager and click Add roles and features directly from the main dashboard. Click Next on the introductory screen.

2.Select the Installation Type

Choose Role-based or feature-based installation, click Next, and select your target server from the local server pool.

3.Add Active Directory Domain Services:

In the Server Roles list, check the box next to Active Directory Domain Services. A prompt will appear asking to add features that are required for AD DS; click Add Features to include the necessary management tools, then click Next through the remaining screens and hit Install.

4.Initiate Domain Controller Promotion

Once the initial role installation finishes successfully, click the notification flag (the yellow warning triangle) at the top right of Server Manager and select Promote this server to a domain controller.

5.Configure the Deployment Operation

For a brand-new environment, select Add a new forest. In the Root domain name field, enter your desired domain structure (e.g., corp.yourdomain.local) and click Next.

6.Set the DSRM Password

Leave the Forest and Domain functional levels at their Windows Server 2025 defaults. Type and confirm a strong Directory Services Restore Mode (DSRM) password. You will need this credential exclusively for disaster recovery scenarios.

7.Finalize and Install

Click Next to skip the DNS delegation warning (this is normal for a new forest) and confirm the auto-generated NetBIOS domain name. Review the default file paths for the NTDS database, logs, and SYSVOL. Continue to the Prerequisites Check, and once all checks pass, click Install. The server will automatically reboot to finalize the configuration.

Once the server reboots, the default login screen will route you to the new domain, completing your setup.

title: How to Install Active Directory on Ubuntu Server
summary: Deploying an Active Directory Domain Controller (AD DC) on Ubuntu Server is entirely possible without Windows Server, thanks to the power of Samba4. Samba4 mimics a Windows Server Active Directory environment, allowing you to centrally manage users, computers, group policies, and DNS.
content:
Deploying an Active Directory Domain Controller (AD DC) on Ubuntu Server is entirely possible without Windows Server, thanks to the power of Samba4. Samba4 mimics a Windows Server Active Directory environment, allowing you to centrally manage users, computers, group policies, and DNS.

Setting this up requires configuring static networking, installing the proper backend tools, and provisioning the domain through Samba’s deployment suite.

Step 1: Update and Configure Server Hostname

Ensure your Ubuntu Server has a static IP. Once configured, establish a Fully Qualified Domain Name (FQDN) for the server. Set your hostname (e.g., dc1) and map it to your local IP address:

javascript 
sudo hostnamectl set-hostname dc1

Edit your /etc/hosts file and map your static IP (e.g., 192.168.1.10) to your intended FQDN and short hostname:

javascript 
# /etc/hosts
192.168.1.10 dc1.corp.example.com dc1

Run system updates to ensure your repository is current:

javascript 
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y

Step 2: Install Samba and Active Directory Packages

Because Linux lacks native Active Directory features, install Samba along with Kerberos client utilities and standard network backend interfaces. During this installation, you will be prompted to enter your default Kerberos realm—enter it in ALL CAPS (e.g., CORP.EXAMPLE.COM).

javascript 
sudo apt install samba krb5-user krb5-config winbind libpam-winbind libnss-winbind libpam-krb5 libpam-ccreds -y

Step 3: Remove Default Configurations

Before provisioning Samba as an AD DC, remove or backup the default smb.conf. This step is critical because the provisioning tool requires a clean slate to build a directory from scratch:

javascript 
sudo systemctl stop smbd nmbd winbind
sudo systemctl disable smbd nmbd winbind
sudo mv /etc/samba/smb.conf /etc/samba/smb.conf.original

Step 4: Provision the Samba Active Directory Domain Controller

Provision the AD DC using the samba-tool utility. Using the --interactive flag will guide you through domain naming, DNS backend choice, and password generation:

javascript 
sudo samba-tool domain provision --use-rfc2307 --interactive
Quick reference input defaults:
  • Realm: CORP.EXAMPLE.COM (Ensure this is in UPPERCASE)
  • Domain: CORP
  • Server Role: dc
  • DNS Backend: SAMBA_INTERNAL
  • DNS Forwarder IP: 8.8.8.8 (or your internal router IP)
  • Administrator Password: Keep it complex to meet standard AD requirements.

Step 5: Link generated Kerberos Configuration

The provisioning process generates an active Kerberos server file. Link it over Ubuntu's system-wide authentication directory:

javascript 
sudo cp /var/lib/samba/private/krb5.conf /etc/krb5.conf

Step 6: Unmask & Enable the AD DC Service

With Windows AD emulated services ready to start, enable and launch the specialized Samba AD Domain Controller daemon:

javascript 
sudo systemctl unmask samba-ad-dc
sudo systemctl enable samba-ad-dc --now

Verify it is running:

javascript 
sudo systemctl status samba-ad-dc

Step 7: Configure DNS Resolvers

Disable systemd-resolved to prevent local DNS override conflicts, and point your network configurations to query local Samba DNS:

javascript 
sudo systemctl disable --now systemd-resolved
sudo rm /etc/resolv.conf

Write a new static resolv.conf pointing to the loopback IP:

javascript 
nameserver 127.0.0.1
search corp.example.com

Step 8: Perform Directory Audits

Test that DNS, domain levels, and authenticate with Kerberos are performing optimally:

javascript 
# Verify domain functional level
sudo samba-tool domain level show

# Authenticate Kerberos tickets
kinit administrator@CORP.EXAMPLE.COM

# List Active Tickets
klist
